summary: The note describes the disposable soma theory of aging, formulated by Thomas Kirkwood, which holds that limited resources force a trade-off between growth, reproduction, and DNA repair, so greater investment in growth and reproduction leaves less for maintenance and drives aging. It reviews the mechanisms (IGF-1/FOXO, mTOR, telomeres, ERCs), evidence from animal and human studies, and criticisms including caloric restriction, the grandmother hypothesis, naked mole rats, and sex biases. The note states that the growth-aging trade-off is well supported while the reproduction-aging link lacks scientific consensus.
one_line: Disposable soma theory holds that aging results from an evolutionary trade-off between growth, reproduction, and DNA repair, and reviews its supporting evidence and criticisms.
key_facts: The disposable soma theory of aging was formulated by Thomas Kirkwood, who first proposed it in a 1977 Nature review article.
Leslie Orgel's Error Catastrophe Theory of Aging was published in 1963 and inspired Kirkwood's theory.

The theory states that greater investment in growth and reproduction results in reduced investment in DNA repair maintenance, leading to cellular damage, shortened telomeres, accumulation of mutations, compromised stem cells, and senescence.
Repair costs are categorized into three groups: the costs of increased durability of nonrenewable parts, the costs of maintenance involving cell renewal, and the costs of intracellular maintenance.
IGF-1 binds a cell receptor and leads to phosphorylation that deactivates FOXO, preventing expression of genes for antioxidants, chaperones, and heat-shock proteins.
In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs) accumulate in mother cells and eventually trigger replicative senescence and death of the mother cell.
Snell and Ames dwarf mice carry mutations that render them incapable of producing IGF-1 or unable to have adequate IGF-1 receptors.
Chihuahuas (average lifespan 15–20 years) have the B/B genotype for the IGF-1 haplotype, while Great Danes (average lifespan 6–8 years) are homozygous for the IGF-1 I allele.
A 1999 study found that administering growth hormone to humans significantly increased mortality rate, after a 1990 study had suggested it reversed aging biomarkers.

In red squirrels, early primiparity yielded the highest reproductive success but a decreased median and maximum lifespan; the average maximum lifespan was 1035 days for early breeders versus 1245 days for late breeders.
In a fruit fly study, the ovoD1 mutation causing defective oogenesis eliminated the lifespan difference between early- and late-reproducing lines.
Steven Austad's 1993 study on opossums from the mainland and predator-absent Sapelo island found the isolated island population had a longer lifespan and delayed primiparity.
The naked mole rat has a lifespan of 30 years, about ten times longer than the brown rat's 3 years, and has almost no detected cancer incidence.
Patients with Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome age about seven times faster than average and usually succumb in their early teens.

Kirkwood and Darryl P. Shanley assert that caloric restriction triggers an adaptive mechanism shifting resources toward somatic maintenance away from reproduction, with SIRT-1 upregulated during low-nutrient periods.
The grandmother hypothesis states that menopause restricts the time of reproduction in older women, allowing them to live longer and care for grandchildren.

entities.name: Disposable soma theory of aging
entities.role: Evolutionary theory that aging results from a trade-off between growth, reproduction, and DNA repair maintenance; the subject of the note

entities.name: Thomas Kirkwood
entities.role: British biologist who first proposed the disposable soma theory in a 1977 Nature review article

entities.name: Leslie Orgel
entities.role: Researcher whose Error Catastrophe Theory of Aging (1963) inspired the disposable soma theory

entities.name: Error Catastrophe Theory of Aging
entities.role: Orgel's 1963 theory that aging arises from mutations acquired during replication

entities.name: Darryl P. Shanley
entities.role: Collaborator of Thomas Kirkwood who asserts caloric restriction shifts resources toward somatic maintenance

entities.name: Steven Austad
entities.role: Aging researcher who performed a 1993 ecological study on opossum populations off the coast of Georgia

entities.name: Sapelo
entities.role: Predator-absent island near the Georgia coast where an isolated opossum population was studied

entities.name: IGF-1 pathway
entities.role: Signaling pathway in which IGF-1 represses FOXO and stimulates mTOR, linked to reduced somatic maintenance and aging

entities.name: FOXO
entities.role: Forkhead transcription factor deactivated by IGF-1 signaling, preventing expression of stress response genes

entities.name: mTOR pathway
entities.role: Pathway stimulated by IGF-1 that promotes protein synthesis and inhibits autophagy

entities.name: Snell and Ames mice
entities.role: Dwarf mouse models with mutations affecting IGF-1 production or receptors

entities.name: Laron syndrome
entities.role: Autosomal recessive disorder causing dwarfism from growth hormone receptor defects; affected individuals have increased lifespan

entities.name: Naked mole rat
entities.role: Rodent species with a 30-year lifespan and efficient cellular repair mechanisms, considered an atypical contradicting model

entities.name: Brown rat
entities.role: Rodent species with a 3-year lifespan used for comparison with naked mole rats

entities.name: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS)
entities.role: Condition causing premature aging, with cellular defects in lamin proteins

entities.name: Sirtuin 1 (SIRT-1)
entities.role: NAD-dependent deacetylase upregulated during low-nutrient periods that increases insulin sensitivity and stimulates autophagy

entities.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
entities.role: Unicellular yeast in which extrachromosomal rDNA circles accumulate in mother cells

entities.name: Grandmother hypothesis
entities.role: Hypothesis that menopause evolved to restrict reproduction time, allowing women to live longer and care for grandchildren

entities.name: Chihuahua
entities.role: Small dog breed with average lifespan of 15–20 years and the B/B IGF-1 haplotype genotype

entities.name: Great Dane
entities.role: Large dog breed with average lifespan of 6–8 years, homozygous for the IGF-1 I allele
